questions.question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Hire
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Engage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Hire"** means to employ someone or to pay someone for their services. (नियुक्त करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The company decided to hire a new manager for their marketing department.
 
 
• **"Engage"** refers to involving or employing someone or something in an activity. It can also mean to occupy attention or interest. (नियुक्त करना)
 
 
• **Example:** The teacher engaged the students in an interactive discussion.
 
 
• Hence, the word "Hire" is synonymous with "Engage".

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Engage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Enhance** (बढ़ाना): To improve or increase the quality, value, or extent of something.
 
 
• **Example:** The company introduced new policies to enhance employee satisfaction.
 
 
• **Engross** (मग्न करना): To completely occupy someone’s attention or focus.
 
 
• **Example:** He was engrossed in the book and didn’t notice the time passing.
 
 
• **Endure** (सहन करना): To suffer through something painful or difficult over a period of time.
 
 
• **Example:** She had to endure a long wait before her turn came.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence from the given options.

options.text: She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes was dirtier.
She was not allow to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirtier.
She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes were dirty.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is written in the past tense, so the correct verb form is **"was not allowed"**, which is grammatically correct.
 
• The subject **"clothes"** is plural, so the verb must agree with it: **"were dirty"** is correct.
 
• The adjective **"dirty"** appropriately describes the state of the clothes without implying unnecessary comparison.
 
• This makes the sentence complete, accurate, and grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She was not allowed to enter the hotel as her clothes **were dirty**."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Her clothes was dirtier" — Incorrect subject-verb agreement ("clothes" is plural, should be "were").
 
• **Option 2:** "She was not allow" — Incorrect verb form; should be "allowed."
 
• **Option 3:** "Were dirtier" — The word "dirtier" implies a comparison, but no comparison is provided in the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the highlighted text in the given sentence.

The minister was** in partnership** with the queen in poisoning the King.

• The word **"in partnership"** used in the sentence implies collaboration or working together, often with a hint of secrecy or conspiracy. (साझेदारी)

 
 
• **Example:** The two companies were in partnership to create a new product.
 
 
 
• **"In cahoots"** means being in secret agreement or conspiracy, typically for a dishonest purpose. (सांठगांठ में)
 
 
• **Example:** The robbers were in cahoots with the security guard to execute the theft.

• **Example:** After losing the game, he was in the blues for the entire evening.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Pankaj is a __better__ cook.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "**Pankaj is a better cook**" is already grammatically correct and uses the appropriate comparative degree of the adjective "good."
 
• "Better" is the correct comparative form of "good" (Good → Better → Best).
 
• The word "better" is used to compare two entities, which may be explicit or implicit in the context. No correction is needed here.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Pankaj is a better cook."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "more good"** — Incorrect. "More good" is not standard English; use "better" instead.
 
• **Option 2: "goodest"** — Incorrect. "Good" is an irregular adjective and does not form its superlative by adding "-est".
 
• **Option 4: "best"** — Incorrect here as "best" is the superlative form used when comparing more than two people or things.

questions.question:
Read the following sentence and select its future tense form from the options given below:

Rachel and Rahul joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.

options.text: Rachel and Rahul are joining forces on a project and successfully completing it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul should join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.
Rachel and Rahul have joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e. Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence provided is in the past tense: "Rachel and Rahul joined forces on a project and successfully completed it within a month."
 
• The task is to convert the sentence into its future tense form.
 
• Future tense typically uses "will" followed by the base form of the verb.

Correct sentence: *Rachel and Rahul will join forces on a project and successfully complete it within a month.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Future Tense:**
 
 
• **Structure:** Subject + will + base verb.
 
• **Example:** She will visit her grandmother tomorrow.
 
• **Usage:** Describes actions or events that are expected to happen in the future.
 
 
 
• **Other Tenses:**
 
 
• **Present Continuous:** "Rachel and Rahul are joining forces..." indicates an ongoing action in the present.
 
• **Past Perfect:** "Rachel and Rahul have joined forces..." refers to actions completed before a certain point in the past.
 
• **Modal 'Should':** "Rachel and Rahul should join forces..." suggests advice or a recommendation, not a future action.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

The teacher asked the students to remain ___, but the noise continued to ___. She finally had to raise her voice to gain control.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**calm; escalate**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"calm"** means quiet or peaceful, which fits the teacher's instruction to the students.
 
• The word **"escalate"** means to increase or intensify, which correctly describes how the noise continued.
 
• Other options like "still; elevate," "silent; ascend," and "quit; rise" are not as contextually appropriate.

​Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *The teacher asked the students to remain calm__, but the noise continued to __escalate__. She finally had to raise her voice to gain control.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Still (स्थिर)**: means motionless, not suitable here with "elevate".
 
• **Silent (मौन)**: means no sound, but "ascend" (go up) is not contextually right for noise.
 
• **Quit (त्यागना)**: means to stop, which is not appropriate in this context with "rise".

 You need to rest the ________ before baking the bread.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**' i.e. **dough**.

• The word **"dough"** refers to a mixture of flour, water, and other ingredients that is kneaded and left to rise before being baked into bread. (आटा गूंथा हुआ)
 
• Letting the dough rest allows fermentation and gluten development, which is crucial for good bread texture.
 
• Hence, the correct and commonly used word in the context of baking is **"dough"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *You need to rest the **dough**__ before baking the bread.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

• **Example:** A doe and her fawn were spotted in the meadow.
 
 
 
• **Lard** (चर्बी): Refers to pig fat used in cooking. It is sometimes used in pastry but is not what you rest before baking bread.
 
 
• **Example:** The pie crust was made flaky with the help of lard.
 
 
 
• **Paste** (लेप/पेस्ट): A general term for a thick, soft mixture, not specific to bread-making.
 
 
• **Example:** He applied a herbal paste to the wound.

questions.question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

Martin Luther King Jr. started a crusade for discrimination ________ African Americans. He relied on peaceful demonstrations and demonstrators. His most famous march was a powerful rally of about 250,000 people in Washington in 1963, where he ________ one of the most famous speeches in history.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**' i.e. **against; delivered**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Against"** is the correct preposition to express opposition to something. (के खिलाफ)
 
• Martin Luther King Jr. fought **against discrimination**, not "versus", "opposed", or "counter" in this structure.
 
• **"Delivered"** is the appropriate verb for giving a speech formally or publicly. (प्रस्तुत किया)
 
• His famous 1963 speech, "I Have a Dream", was **delivered** at the Lincoln Memorial in Washington, D.C.
 
• **Example:** He delivered a historic speech that inspired millions across the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

**Complete Sentence:** *Martin Luther King Jr. started a crusade for discrimination **against**__ African Americans. He relied on peaceful demonstrations and demonstrators. His most famous march was a powerful rally of about 250,000 people in Washington in 1963, where he __**delivered**__ one of the most famous speeches in history.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Opposed; dropped**: "Opposed" is a verb, not suitable after “for discrimination.” "Dropped" is informal and does not fit the context of a historic speech.
 
• **Versus; brought**: "Versus" is used in competitions or comparisons, not for social causes. "Brought" is vague for speech delivery.
 
• **Counter; dispatched**: "Counter" is not grammatically correct here, and "dispatched" refers to sending people or messages, not delivering speeches.

• **Example:** The flowers began to wither in the heat.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I still / do not understand / why he did not / reply my email.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **"reply"** is an **intransitive verb**, which means it does not take a direct object without a preposition.
 
• The correct usage is: **"reply to my email"**, not "reply my email".
 
• So, the segment **"reply my email"** contains the grammatical error due to the missing preposition "to".

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I still do not understand why he did not **reply to** my email."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "why he did not"** – grammatically correct.
 
• **Option 2: "I still"** – grammatically correct and appropriate in context.
 
• **Option 4: "do not understand"** – correct verb usage in present tense.

• In the sentence, Shirin generated a solution — hence, “came up with” is the correct expression.
 
• The original phrase **"came off with"** is incorrect here. "Come off" usually means to succeed or happen, not to generate an idea.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Shirin **came up with**__ a brilliant idea to solve the problem."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "came off on"** – Incorrect and ungrammatical; no such phrasal verb exists in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "came off to"** – Incorrect usage; “come off to” is not used to indicate idea generation.

questions.question: Select the grammatically correct sentence.

options.text: The secondary section of the school is located at the end of the street.
The secondary section of a school is located at the end of a street.
A secondary section of the school is located at an end of the street.
The secondary section of a school is located at an end of the street.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In Option 3, "A secondary section of the school..." refers to a specific part of the school but without implying it's the only one. It correctly uses the indefinite article "**a**" before "secondary section" to indicate that there is one such section in the school, but it doesn't assume that it is the only one.
 
• The use of "at an end of the street" is also appropriate because it refers to a general end of the street, not a specific one.
 
• This sentence is grammatically correct because it doesn't attempt to be overly specific, allowing for the possibility of other secondary sections or ends of the street.

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A secondary section of the school is located at an end of the street."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "The secondary section of the school..." – This implies that there is only one secondary section in the school, which may or may not be the case.
 
• **Option 2:** "The secondary section of a school..." – The indefinite article "a" makes the school non-specific, which could imply any school, not the intended specific school.
 
• **Option 4:** "The secondary section of a school..." – Similar to Option 2, this makes the school non-specific and changes the intended meaning.

questions.question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains as error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Their chance of winning is __slimmest__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective **"slim"** is used to describe the degree or extent of chance without any direct comparison.
 
• The original sentence *"Their chance of winning is slimmest"* is incorrect because it uses the superlative form **"slimmest"** without comparing among three or more alternatives.
 
• In general descriptions (not comparisons), the **positive degree** adjective **"slim"** is appropriate.
 
• Hence, **"Their chance of winning is slim"** is grammatically and contextually correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Their chance of winning is **slim**__."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "slimly"** – Incorrect; it's an adverb and does not fit here to describe a noun ("chance").
 
• **Option 2: "slimmer"** – Comparative form, used only when comparing two entities, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 3: "most slim"** – Awkward and redundant; "slimmest" would be the proper superlative, but again not needed without comparison.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Inferior
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 (Superior)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Inferior"** means of lower quality, rank, or status compared to someone or something else. (अधम, निम्न)

 
 
• **Example:** The quality of this product is inferior to the one I purchased last year.
 
 
 
• **"Superior"** refers to something or someone of higher quality, rank, or status. It is the opposite of inferior. (श्रेष्ठ, उच्च)
 
 
• **Example:** Her performance in the project was superior to everyone else in the team.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can conclude that the antonym of **"Inferior"** is **"Superior"**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 (Superior)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Example:** The builder was fined for using substandard materials in the construction.

• **Example:** The sunset over the mountains was simply beautiful.
 
 
 
• **Mediocre** (सामान्य): Of only moderate quality; not very good.
 
 
• **Example:** His performance in the exam was mediocre, not exceptional.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**focusing**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence reads: "Employers, nowadays, are _______ on team-building..." which clearly indicates the use of the present continuous tense.
 
• The auxiliary verb **“are”** requires the **present participle** form of the verb to complete the tense.
 
• Hence, the correct form is **"focusing"**, making the complete phrase: **"are focusing on team-building..."**
 
• This structure expresses an ongoing trend or action happening at the present time.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Employers, nowadays, **are focusing**__ on team-building as it proves to be useful in being more productive.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Has focused**: Incorrect because it's in the present perfect tense, which does not suit the ongoing nature of the action.
 
• **Focuses**: Incorrect as it is a simple present tense used with singular subjects; 'employers' is plural.
 
• **Focus**: Incorrect as it lacks the correct auxiliary to form present continuous tense.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**of**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct phrase is **"sick of"**, which is a common English expression used to show frustration, annoyance, or boredom with something.
 
• The sentence mentions employees being tired or irritated by office festival parties — making **"sick of"** the most natural and grammatically appropriate choice.
 
• Other prepositions like **"with"**, **"from"**, and **"for"** do not correctly complete the idiomatic expression “sick ___”.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Some employees are **sick of**__ office festival parties with mandatory dress codes and fun competitions.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Sick of**: Means annoyed, bored, or fed up with something — correct usage here.
 
• **Sick with**: Generally used for illnesses (e.g., sick with flu) — incorrect in this context.
 
• **Sick from**: Used to indicate cause of illness — not appropriate here.
 
• **Sick for**: Rarely used and does not fit idiomatically in this sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**are tired**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The subject of the sentence is **"Some others"**, which is a plural noun phrase.
 
• To match the plural subject, we need a plural verb — hence, **"are tired"** is the grammatically correct choice.
 
• The phrase "**are tired of**" is a common expression used to convey boredom or frustration with a repeated activity or situation.
 
• Other options either have incorrect subject-verb agreement ("has tired", "have tired") or do not maintain correct tense or structure ("tired" alone is incomplete as a verb form).

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *Some others **are tired**__ of having to forcibly bond with colleagues during after-work happy hours when they would rather be at home.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Tired**: Not a complete verb on its own in this structure; needs a helping verb.
 
• **Has tired**: Incorrect subject-verb agreement (used with singular subjects, not "some others").
 
• **Have tired**: Grammatically awkward and unnatural in this context; implies causing someone else to be tired, not the subject being tired.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**has ruled**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to a recent action by a French court, which requires the use of the **present perfect tense** to indicate a past event with present relevance.
 
• **“Has ruled”** is the correct form for a singular subject (“court”) in the present perfect tense.
 
• It correctly communicates that the ruling happened recently and has ongoing implications.
 
• Other options like **"is ruled"** (present passive), **"have ruled"** (plural subject), and **"was ruled"** (simple past passive) are grammatically or contextually incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *A French court **has ruled**__ recently that one very much has the right to be boring at the workplace.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Is ruled**: Incorrect tense and passive voice — doesn’t fit the context.
 
• **Have ruled**: Incorrect because "court" is singular; "have" is for plural subjects.
 
• **Was ruled**: Incorrect past passive construction; suggests the court itself was ruled over.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**violated**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence refers to a past event, i.e., the court's ruling that took place after Mr. T was fired from his company.
 
• Therefore, the verb should also be in the **past tense** to maintain proper grammatical consistency.
 
• The court stated that the company’s culture of fun **violated** Mr. T’s fundamental rights — this action is viewed in retrospect.
 
• Other options like **"violate"** (present), **"will violate"** (future), and **"is violated"** (present passive) do not fit the past narrative context of the passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

Complete Sentence: *It added that the company’s culture of fun **violated**__ Mr. T’s fundamental right to ‘dignity and respect of private life’.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Violate**: Present tense — incorrect as the ruling refers to a past action.
 
• **Will violate**: Future tense — doesn't match the past action referenced.
 
• **Is violated**: Present passive — incorrect structure for past incident.
